chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Hamza who said:

Nafi' ibn al-Azraq asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and said: 'Inform me about God — when did He exist?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'When did He not exist, that I may inform you when He existed? Glory be to the One who never ceased to be and will never cease to be, Singular, the Eternal Refuge, who took neither a female companion nor a son.'

key_terms.سُبْحَانَ: Subhan — glorification/exaltation of God, indicating transcendence beyond all imperfection.
key_terms.صَمَداً: Samad — often translated 'Eternal Refuge' or 'the Self-Sufficient Master'; a divine name appearing in Quran 112:2. It denotes the One to whom all creation turns in need, and who is in need of nothing.
key_terms.فَرْداً: Fard — absolutely singular, without peer or partner. This is a Divine attribute of uniqueness.
key_terms.لَمْ يَزَلْ وَلَا يَزَالُ: Never ceased to be and will never cease to be — a classical Islamic formulation of God's eternal pre-existence (azaliyya) and everlastingness (abadiyya).

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir say when asked 'when did Allah exist?'
ai.summary: Nafi' ibn al-Azraq, a Kharijite leader known for theological disputations, posed the question 'when did Allah exist?' to Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him). The Imam's response brilliantly inverts the question: asking when God was NOT is meaningless, because His existence is eternal and unconditioned by time. The Imam then glorifies God with attributes echoing Surah al-Ikhlas: singular (fard), the eternal refuge (samad), without partner or offspring.
